newsitem.title: UK: KwikSave jumps on vague merger talk.
newsitem.headline: KwikSave jumps on vague merger talk.

text.p: Shares in food retailer KwikSave Plc rose sharply on Wednesday amid vague talk that the group may be contemplating a merger with frozen food store group Iceland, traders said.
But many were sceptical of the talk, despite the 21p rise in KwikSave shares to 332-1/2p and Iceland's 5p gain to 91-1/2p.
"There are some rumours doing the rounds but I don't believe them. The shares were overclubbed a couple of weeks ago and I think it's just a bit of bottom fishing," said one.
Shares in KwikSave have fallen from 673p over the past year amid falling profits and tough competition.
Iceland Group has also suffered from aggressive competition from big supermarket chains, the shares sliding from 176p in 12 months.

"I never say never about these sort of rumours but the vast majority of cases don't come to anything. If you take two companies that are in trouble and put them together you risk producing a company in twice as much trouble," said one analyst.
The rumour had been around before, said the analyst, but apart from savings on head office overheads -- savings on distribution would be limited.
"The emphasis on both businesses is very different. I don't know that the two combined would do anything for sales," he said.
A spokeswoman for Iceland said it was company policy not to comment on market rumours. No-one at KwikSave was immediately available for comment.
